steps.title: Step 1: Immediate Action (Helplines/Numbers)
steps.content: If you're in an emergency, dial 112 for immediate police assistance. For specific issues, use these helplines: Women Helpline: 1091, Domestic Violence Helpline: 181, National Cybercrime Helpline: 1930, NCW Helpline: 7827170170.

steps.title: Step 2: Official Filing (Links/Portals)
steps.content: Depending on your issue, visit these official portals: For cybercrime complaints, go to https://www.cybercrime.gov.in. For workplace harassment, file a complaint on https://shebox.nic.in/.

data.explanation: Filing a case in court can be a bit overwhelming, but it's an important step to protect your rights and seek justice. Depending on your situation, the process can vary. For example, if you're dealing with domestic violence, cybercrime, or workplace harassment, there are specific steps and portals you need to follow. It's crucial to gather all necessary evidence and follow the correct procedures to ensure your case is handled properly. Remember, you have rights that protect you, and there are helplines and portals designed to assist you through this process.

steps.title: Step 1: Immediate Action (Helplines/Numbers)
steps.content: Depending on your issue, dial the appropriate helpline: Women Helpline (1091) for domestic violence, National Cybercrime Helpline (1930) for cybercrime, or NCW Helpline (7827170170) for workplace harassment.

steps.title: Step 2: Official Filing (Links/Portals)
steps.content: Visit the relevant portal to file your complaint: https://www.cybercrime.gov.in for cybercrime, https://shebox.nic.in/ for workplace harassment, or visit the nearest Protection Officer or 'Mahila Thana' (Women Police Station) for domestic violence.

steps.title: Step 3: Legal/Evidence
steps.content: Gather all necessary evidence. For domestic violence, save photos of injuries and abusive messages. For cybercrime, export WhatsApp chats as.txt, save URL links of profiles, and take screenshots of transaction IDs. For workplace harassment, submit a written complaint to your company's Internal Committee (IC).

data.query: How can I track the status of my FIR?
data.explanation: You've filed an FIR (First Information Report) and now you want to know its status. This is important because the status will tell you if the police are actively investigating your case. Knowing the status can also help you understand the next steps you need to take. It's like checking the progress of an important task you've assigned; you need to know if it's moving forward or if there are any issues.
laws: IPC: Varies based on the nature of the crime
BNS: Varies based on the nature of the crime
rights: Right to information about the status of your FIR
Right to follow up with the police station if there are delays

steps.title: Step 1: Immediate Action (Helplines/Numbers)
steps.content: Dial 100 or visit your nearest police station to inquire about the status of your FIR. You can also contact the police helpline at 112 for assistance.

steps.title: Step 2: Official Filing (Links/Portals)
steps.content: Visit the official police portal of your state to check the status of your FIR. Many states have online services for this purpose. For example, in Delhi, you can visit https://www.delhipolice.nic.in/.

steps.title: Step 3: Legal/Evidence
steps.content: Keep a copy of your FIR acknowledgment receipt. This will have a unique number that you can use to track the status. If you face any issues, you can also contact a legal aid organization for assistance.
